name: aubio
baseline: audioread FFmpegAudioFile (decodes through an ffmpeg subprocess)
workload: Python audio-loading benchmark: time to decode a mono noise file (1 to 151 s long, 16 durations, one file per duration) into a numpy array with aubio.source (hop_size 1024) versus audioread's FFmpegAudioFile, librosa, soundfile and others; a second benchmark times metadata queries (samplerate, channels, samples, duration).
claimed_speedup: Numbers derived from the benchmark's results/*.pickle files in the repo (mean over the 16 durations, seconds for three consecutive loads; ratios derived from page data). Load to numpy, aubio vs audioread+ffmpeg: wav 0.064 vs 0.657 (about 10x), mp4 0.044 vs 0.101 (about 2.3x), mp3 0.068 vs 0.103 (about 1.5x), flac 0.067 vs 0.071 (about 1.06x, a tie). Versus librosa: mp3 0.068 vs 0.131 (about 1.9x), mp4 0.044 vs 0.111 (about 2.5x), wav 0.064 vs 0.289 (about 4.5x). Metadata-only queries, aubio vs audioread: mp3 0.0015 vs 0.098 (about 66x), flac 0.0015 vs 0.098 (about 66x), mp4 0.0030 vs 0.106 (about 35x), ogg 0.0046 vs 0.200 (about 44x), wav 0.040 vs 0.099 (about 2.5x). aubio is slower than other loaders in some rows: flac load 0.067 vs soundfile 0.045 and librosa 0.039; wav load 0.064 vs scipy 0.014; wav metadata 0.040 vs soundfile 0.0008.
tradeoffs: GPL-3.0-or-later, so copyleft for anything linking it. The fast decode path depends on the aubio build having libav (ffmpeg), libsndfile or CoreAudio enabled; the Python API streams hop-sized blocks (loop in Python), so very small hop sizes cost interpreter time. Python package is the code measured, not the C library alone.
caveats: Independent community benchmark (faroit/python_audio_loading_benchmark, 152 stars, last commit 2023-12-19), not run by the aubio project. The README only shows bar charts on a log time axis; the exact numbers above come from the results/benchmark_np_<ext>.pickle and benchmark_metadata_<ext>.pickle files in the repo, read with a restricted unpickler (no code executed). Hardware, CPU model, compiler and build flags are not stated ('our server'), and the aubio package's build configuration (which decoder backend) is not stated, so this falls short of tier A. Harness quirks: the stored time is the minimum over 3 repeats of timeit with number=3 (so seconds for 3 loads, not 1), and only the last file of each duration folder is recorded (one file per duration). The audioread baseline spawns an ffmpeg process per file, so aubio's win over it is largely process-spawn overhead rather than faster codecs; aubio itself decodes mp3/mp4 through libav when built with it. Versus libsndfile (soundfile) and scipy aubio is slower for wav and flac, so aubio is a competitive loader rather than the fastest one. aubio's own repo has only python/demos/demo_reading_speed.py with no published numbers, and its README makes no speed claim. The 'ffmpeg or standard codec' baseline is a Haiku guess; the row compared here is audioread's FFmpeg wrapper, not the ffmpeg library called from C.
